title: Fast logical operations in quantum LDPC codes using simple resource states
abstract: Quantum LPDC codes provide a substantial reduction in qubit overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum computation compared to surface code, thanks to their high encoding rate. However, operating simultaneously on multiple logical qubits encoded in the same block is more challenging and may slow down logical operations. Prior work addresses this problem by designing complex resource states to perform logical measurements in LDPC codes. Here, we propose an approach that only consumes cat states. Whereas previous work on cat-based measurements focuses on a single logical measurement, we design a protocol for the joint measurement of $\ell$ commuting logical operators. The key ingredient is the design of a scheduler code determining the measurement sequence and allowing for the decoding of all logical measurement outcomes. Numerical simulations with the LDPC codes Q70 and Q102 of the walking cat architecture show a speed-up of nearly $3\times$ over Viterbi measurements for the measurement of $\ell=20$ commuting logical operators. Combining our fast logical measurements with a new variant of the CliNR partial error correction scheme, we achieve a speed up of up to up to $74\times$ for random Clifford circuits. Our approach also applies to non-Clifford gates, producing a speed up of up to $5\times$ for Toffoli gates.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, resource-efficient method for performing joint logical measurements in quantum LDPC codes by utilizing only cat states. By introducing a scheduler code, the authors significantly accelerate the process of implementing complex gates like Clifford and Toffoli circuits compared to previous state-of-the-art methods. This work is crucial for advancing the feasibility and speed of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop significantly faster protocols for performing joint logical measurements of multiple commuting Pauli operators within quantum LDPC codes.
main_result: The proposed cat-state measurement approach achieves up to a $74	imes$ speed-up over Viterbi measurements for random Clifford circuits, and shows substantial gains for Toffoli gates as well.
method: The authors propose using a scheduler code to manage the joint measurement sequence of $\ell$ commuting operators, relying solely on cat states rather than complex resource states used in prior work.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum LDPC codes, specifically mentioning implementations suitable for platforms like trapped ions or neutral atoms (the 'walking cat architecture'). The operations involve implementing logical Clifford and Toffoli gates via the CliNR partial error correction scheme.
key_observables: Speed-up factor compared to Viterbi measurements; Logical Measurement Counts ($	ext{LM}$) and Cat-based Measurement Counts ($	ext{CM}$); Logical Error Rate ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: $\ell$ (number of commuting operators), code sizes (Q70, Q102), target error rates ($10^{-10}$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that fault-tolerance is not required to achieve the target logical error rate for a specific algorithm, and it utilizes specialized scheduler codes.
figures_summary: Table IV compares Logical Measurements (LM) and Cat-based Measurements (CM) across Viterbi gate-based, Viterbi CliNR, and MEDM CliNR protocols for Toffoli circuits and random Cliffords.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of fast logical operations in LDPC codes. It details the proposed cat-state measurement protocol using a scheduler code (MEDM/MECM). The core argument involves comparing this new method against established Viterbi protocols for implementing logical Clifford gates via CliNR, culminating in quantitative speed-up results.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract quantum coding theory, the underlying concepts of resource state management and efficient measurement scheduling are highly relevant to designing practical fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures using physical platforms like trapped ions or superconducting qubits.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Physical and Logical CliNR Circuits: in physical CliNR, resource state preparation (RSP) and verification (RSV) are separate steps followed by injection (RSI). In logical CliNR, RSP and RSV are merged and implemented at the logical level and RSI is implemented at the physical level.

FIG. 2: Viterbi Gate-Based Protocol for implementing Clifford operations. We illustrate the protocol using a circuit composed of CNOT and CZ gates. Each logical CNOT between control qubit C and target qubit T is implemented using a logical auxiliary qubit A and three Pauli measurements. Each Pauli measurement employs the Viterbi measurement protocol which requires on average 5.06 cat-based measurements for our default error rate parameters.
